extracted.intended_audience: Prospective NEH grant applicants (and others preparing applications to National Endowment for the Humanities grant programs)
extracted.subtask_description: Describes how the National Endowment for the Humanities evaluates grant applications across its programs, including rating scale, universal and common review criteria, multi-level review steps, and feedback practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluators choose from the following ratings: E - Excellent; VG - Very Good; G - Good; SM - Some Merit; NC - Not Competitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These standardized shorthand ratings are used by evaluators to indicate overall merit. Applicants may request to see the evaluators' ratings for their application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a universal review criterion that reviews will generally always address; refers to the importance or intellectual impact of the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A universal review criterion; assesses novelty, fresh perspectives, or unique contributions to the humanities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A universal review criterion; evaluates whether the proposed plan, timeline, and resources make successful completion likely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Intellectual significance of the proposed project, including its value to humanities scholars, general audiences, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical NEH criterion assessing who benefits from the project and the depth or breadth of its contribution to scholarship and/or public understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of conception and methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of the conception, definition, organization, and description of the project, and the soundness of methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates clarity of project design, appropriateness and rigor of methods, and thoroughness of project planning and documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Likelihood of completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Likelihood of completion in a reasonable time frame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses whether the scope, schedule, staffing, and resources are realistic for finishing the project within the proposed timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of staff/expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of the staff, including expertise in the relevant scholarly fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers qualifications, track record, and capacity of project personnel to carry out the proposed work successfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonableness of budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasonableness of the budget in relation to the proposed activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates whether budgeted costs are appropriate, justified, and proportionate to the project scope and planned activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-level NEH review process (roles and steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH's review process has FOUR distinct but fully integrated levels: knowledgeable persons independent of the agency read each application; panel discussion; NEH staff organizes and summarizes panel results; NEH staff recommends meritorious applications while maintaining even quality across panels; National Council on the Humanities advises the Chairman, who makes final funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process-level standard describing who evaluates applications and how decisions are made: (1) outside expert readers, (2) reviewer panel discussion, (3) NEH staff synthesis of reviews, (4) NEH staff recommendation balancing merit and panel quality, (5) National Council advising Chairman for final funding decisions. This sequence indicates that application quality is judged both at reader/panel level and then curated by staff and Council before final award determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer feedback and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: All applicants can receive upon request the evaluators' ratings and written comments. NEH does not provide the names of the evaluators with their comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency practice: applicants may obtain reviewers' assessments but reviewer identities remain confidential. This affects how applicants interpret feedback (ratings/comments without reviewer attribution).
